Title: Brunei, Malaysia to strengthen cross-border security, SAR cooperation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Brunei have agreed to strengthen cooperation in addressing cross-border security issues, including the smuggling of contraband and other illegal activities, as well as search and rescue (SAR) and emergency response.
In a joint statement issued by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Sultan of Brunei Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah following the 27th Annual Leaders' Consultation between the two countries in Bandar Seri Begawan, the two leaders said cross-border security issues needed to be addressed through closer cooperation between the relevant agencies of both sides.
"In this regard, the Working Committee on Security Matters Related to the Brunei Darussalam-Malaysia Land Boundary was urged to finalise the draft Guidelines on the Sharing of Information and Designation of Contact Points, which would enhance communication and coordination between both countries."
On cross-border SAR and emergency response, both leaders said the focus would be on enhancing coordination, exploring areas of collaboration and strengthening mutual understanding of cross-border arrangements, while building on existing cooperation in disaster management.
Both leaders also acknowledged the importance of closer coordination in addressing cross-border disaster management and emergency response.
In this regard, they welcomed the renewal of the Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation in Disaster Management today.
Anwar and Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah also acknowledged the continued discussions on maritime-related matters.
In this regard, the leaders recalled the agreement at last year's annual leaders' consultation to establish a joint ad hoc committee on maritime-related matters and encouraged both sides to finalise the Terms of Reference for the effective implementation of maritime issues under the 2009 Exchange of Letters (EOL).

Title: China, Indonesia deepen defence ties, cooperation on minerals, energy and tech
Article:
JAKARTA: China and Indonesia agreed on Friday to boost military ties and work closely on minerals, energy and technology, as Jakarta seeks to balance ties with both Beijing and Washington amid economic and geopolitical tensions, including in the South China Sea.
Both countries should "seize the moment," China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi said in remarksmade at the start of his visit to Jakarta. He was travelling with Defence Minister Dong Jun to meet their Indonesian counterparts.
"The current international situation is intertwined and complex. Unilateralism and hegemonic acts bring serious impact on global cooperation and stability," he said.
"China actively aims to build China-Indonesia cooperation at a high level," Wang added.
The two countries pledged to cooperate across multiple areas from artificial intelligence, defence and rail transport to green energy, satellites and fisheries. Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto has advocated maintaining Indonesia's "free and active" foreign policy of non-alignment, vowing to befriend all countries including China and the United States, an important trade partner with which Jakarta's defence ties are expanding.
Wang said both sides agreed to support each other's core interests and will cooperate more in energy and mineral resources.
Resource-rich Indonesia, a US$1.4 trillion G20 economy, has vast deposits of nickel, tin, copper, gold and bauxite and is the world's largest exporter of palm oil and of thermal coal, with China among its top buyers. China dominates investment in Indonesia's nickel processing sector, but recent policy changes, including on exports and tighter mining quotas, have pushed some companies to seek alternative supplies elsewhere.
HIGHER-QUALITY COOPERATION
Chinese Defence Minister Dong was greeted on Friday by a military guard of honour as he arrived for talks with his Indonesian counterpart Sjafrie Sjamsoeddin.
"The prospects for cooperation between the two militaries are broad, and that such cooperation is becoming higher in quality and more effective," Dong said.
Sjafrie said there would be increased defence activities between their militaries, including joint exercises and officer exchanges.
Later, after a meeting between the defence and foreign ministers of both countries, Sjafrie told reporters that they also discussed a joint munitions factory in Indonesia, producing ammunition, missiles and rockets and including a possible transfer of technology from China. The factory is expected to start operation by 2027.
"This is a progressive step taken in the era of building Indonesia's defence power at this moment and in the future," he said. Last week, Taiwan, which China claims as its own territory, was angered by a rare joint military exercise between the Chinese and Indonesian navies that took place east of Taiwan.
Indonesia's navy said a vessel conducted routine exercises, not only with China, but also with Japan and the United States.
Defence analyst Curie Maharani said that while Indonesia saw the exercise as routine, the location enabled China to signal a different political message.
"Indonesia learned a valuable lesson about how great powers use defence diplomacy more as an instrument of influence projection," she said.
Indonesia also has its own disagreements with China over developments in the South China Sea, which Beijing claims almost in its entirety. Jakarta has been measured in its remarks, however, and sees itself as not being party to wider territorial disputes involving China and the Philippines, Malaysia and Vietnam.
TRADE AND INVESTMENT
China is a major investor in Indonesia, contributing US$3.9 billion of foreign direct investment in the first half of 2026, according to Indonesian figures. But regulations around some of that investment have been a source of friction.
In May, Chinese companies operating in Indonesia urged the government to adopt more business-friendly policies, complaining about higher taxes and a new nickel pricing formula.
In a letter seen by Reuters, the China Chamber ​of Commerce in Indonesia said Chinese firms faced "excessively stringent regulation, over-enforcement", and ⁠alleged corruption and extortion by authorities.
Key investors include the world's biggest EV battery maker, Contemporary Amperex Technology, and steelmaker Tsingshan Group, which has smelters in Indonesia.--REUTERS

Title: Malaysia, Brunei target 2034 to complete border demarcation, Sector F-G by 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Brunei have agreed to jointly determine and demarcate the watershed in Sector F-G of their land boundary by May 31 next year, reaffirming that the issue must be resolved solely based on the watershed principle.
In a joint statement, both leaders reiterated their commitment to the 2009 Exchange of Letters and other bilateral instruments governing the demarcation and survey of the land boundary.
"The resolution of Sector F-G must be based solely on the watershed principle," the statement said, adding that both countries had agreed to jointly determine a single watershed in the sector.
The agreement was reached during the 27th Annual Leaders' Consultation between Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Sultan of Brunei Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah today.
The leaders also set May 31, 2027, as the deadline to complete the survey and demarcation, in accordance with the 2024 Exchange of Notes.
They noted discussions under existing bilateral mechanisms, including the 20th Technical Committee Meeting on the Demarcation and Survey of the Land Boundary, held in Penang in June, and the fifth meeting of the Joint Malaysia-Brunei Darussalam Land Boundary Committee, held in Putrajaya earlier this month.
The leaders urged the Joint Technical Committee to accelerate technical work on all outstanding sectors, particularly those identified as priorities, while taking into account points of convergence between both sides.
Malaysia and Brunei are also targeting completion of the joint survey and demarcation of their entire land boundary by 2034.
To date, 264.791km, or about 50 per cent of the boundary, has been jointly surveyed and demarcated.
Under the 2009 Exchange of Letters, the 2012 Memorandum of Understanding on the Process for the Joint Demarcation and Survey of the Land Boundary and its accompanying Terms of Reference, undelimited or undemarcated sections are to be resolved based on the existing five Land Boundary Agreements.
"Where no agreement exists, the two countries are to negotiate solely on the basis of the watershed principle."
Also present were Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg, Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor, Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
The 27th Annual Leaders' Consultation is the highest-level bilateral mechanism between Malaysia and Brunei, providing a platform for the two sides to review bilateral cooperation and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest.
In 2025, total trade between Malaysia and Brunei was recorded at RM5.86 billion (US$1.37 billion), with exports to Brunei valued at RM4.20 billion (US$0.98 billion) and imports at RM1.66 billion (US$0.39 billion).
For January to June 2026, total trade between the two countries reached RM2.38 billion (US$600 million).

Title: AUKU repeal to pave way for new higher education law
Article:
KEPALA BATAS: The repeal of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) is not solely focused on students, as the government is also reviewing the entire higher education legal framework before introducing a new Act as its replacement.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the review was necessary as AUKU is the main legislation governing not only student-related matters but also the establishment and operations of universities, governance, academic affairs and administration.
"AUKU currently has 44 sections covering aspects such as university establishment, governance, academic matters, academics, administrators and other areas, with only seven sections related to students.
"In the context of students, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has emphasised that we need to examine aspects that have become constraints," he told reporters after opening the Tun Abdullah Ahmad Badawi Cancer Centre (PKTAAB) at Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) here today.
Zambry said the review would take into account the freedom and rights of academics, challenges faced by them, as well as the needs of administrators, students, institutions and other laws related to the country's higher education system.
He said the new Act must serve as the main legal framework covering the entire higher education ecosystem, addressing both present and future needs.
The minister said the independent committee announced earlier would allow various views to be considered during the review process, in line with the government's commitment to listen to all parties before finalising the new legal framework.
Zambry
was reported as saying that a more comprehensive higher education legal framework to replace AUKU had been outlined under the Malaysia Higher Education Blueprint (RPTM) 2026-2035, as part of the agenda to establish the One Higher Education Act launched in January.
Previously, Anwar said the government would repeal AUKU to provide greater freedom and democratic space for students, after considering memorandums and views submitted by student leaders seeking comprehensive changes to the Act.

Title: Kuantan jewellery heist over in 5 minutes, getaway bikes had no number plates
Article:
KUANTAN: Four armed men took just five minutes to make off with RM500,000 worth of jewellery from a goldsmith's shop in Taman Pandan Damai here yesterday.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Ashari Abu Samah said the masked suspects arrived and fled on two motorcycles without number plates, believed to be part of an attempt to evade identification.
"There were no customers during the incident, only the shop owner's wife and two female employees. The suspects were inside for about five minutes before fleeing," he said when contacted today.
Ashari said police were reviewing closed-circuit television footage from nearby premises and dashcam recordings to determine whether the suspects abandoned their motorcycles and switched to other vehicles.
Yesterday,
the four suspects, armed with a parang
and a suspected pump-action gun, entered the shop about 2pm and fled with jewellery worth RM500,000.
The suspects left their motorcycles outside before entering the half-shop lot. There was no security guard on duty, while police have yet to determine whether the alarm was triggered.
Police are also tracing the suspects' escape routes, as they may not have travelled far on the motorcycles, and investigating whether they had accomplices.
The robbery was the
second armed heist
reported in Pahang this week, following the Aug 17 robbery in Genting Highlands, Bentong, where three men fled with jewellery worth RM1.7 million. The suspects remain at large.

Title: After past mishap, 88-year-old Melaka man takes no chances with Jalur Gemilang
Article:
MELAKA: An 88-year-old Melaka man is taking no chances with the Jalur Gemilang this National Month, repeatedly contacting his assemblyman to ensure the national flag at his home is not displayed upside down again.
George Lim, a Baba Nyonya from Taman Semabok Jaya, contacted Duyong assemblyman Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem more than five times after a previous experience of having the Jalur Gemilang installed incorrectly left him deeply concerned about a repeat of the mistake.
Noor Helmy said Lim remained traumatised by the previous incident but was determined to continue flying the national flag at his home.
"He called me more than five times to make sure the Jalur Gemilang installed at his home would not be displayed incorrectly again.
"Although the previous incident left an impression on him, his determination to fly the national flag at home has never wavered, and that is something worth commending," he said when met recently.
Noor Helmy, who is also deputy chairman of the state executive council committee for Science, Technology, Innovation and Digital Communications, had earlier uploaded a video of his visit to George's home in Taman Semabok Jaya.
He said the visit was made after Lim expressed concern over the installation of the flag and wanted to ensure it was done correctly.
"George's spirit, despite being 88 years old, deserves to be appreciated as he continues to show his love for the country by flying the Jalur Gemilang at his home.
"His Baba Nyonya background has never stopped him from showing his patriotism ahead of the National Month celebrations.
"His repeated efforts to seek confirmation also show how important the Jalur Gemilang is to him as a symbol of the country's sovereignty and identity," he said.
Lim had previously experienced having the national flag installed upside down, but the incident did not deter him from continuing to fly the Jalur Gemilang at his home.

Title: Malaysia, Brunei deepen cooperation in border management, education, disaster response
Article:
BANDAR SERI BEGAWAN: Malaysia and Brunei Darussalam have agreed to strengthen cooperation in various fields, including border management, immigration, education, disaster management, trade and investment.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said long-standing border issues between the two countries were also given priority during his discussions with Sultan of Brunei Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah at Istana Nurul Iman here today.
He said an initial understanding had been reached to ensure that areas agreed to belong to Brunei and Sarawak would be maintained, in line with the interests of both countries.
Anwar said about 50 per cent of the border-related process had been resolved, while the remaining matters yet to be finalised would be examined in detail by the technical committees of both countries.
"Some 50 per cent has been resolved. There are indeed matters among the remaining issues that require further consideration.
"So, we agreed that both sides would find a way to ensure Malaysia's rights and interests are recognised based on the law and boundaries, and likewise for Brunei's rights and interests based on the same factors," he said at a press conference at Brunei International Airport here today after concluding his two-day working visit to Brunei.
Also present were Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg and Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
He said the issue, which had remained unresolved for 60 years, could be settled, with the technical committees required to examine the matter in detail before submitting their findings for further consideration.
He said although the foreign ministers of both countries had initially targeted a resolution by early next year, he and the Sultan of Brunei believed the basic parameters of the matter could be resolved by the end of this year, making the subsequent process merely a formality.
On a related matter, Anwar said Malaysia and Brunei also recognised the need to facilitate the movement of people between the two countries, particularly by reducing repeated inspections at several checkpoints between Brunei, Sarawak and Sabah.
He said the matter would be addressed through technical cooperation between the relevant agencies to ensure smoother cross-border movement, thereby supporting economic and social ties between the two countries.
On the haze issue, Anwar said Malaysia and Brunei had agreed to use the best Asean mechanisms to address the matter, with the relevant ministries to coordinate follow-up action.
"We have sent a letter to the Asean secretary-general, and the relevant minister will coordinate this matter," he said.
On education, Anwar said Universiti Brunei Darussalam currently had strong capabilities and performance, and he would refer the matter of recognition of its qualifications to the Malaysian Qualifications Agency (MQA).
He said the move would allow Malaysian students, particularly those from Sabah, Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, to pursue their studies in Brunei Darussalam, just as Brunei students currently pursue their studies at educational institutions in Malaysia.
He said the matter had previously been delayed due to the degree recognition process, but efforts would be intensified to strengthen educational cooperation between the two countries.
Anwar also said disaster management cooperation between Malaysia and Brunei would be expanded through a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on search and rescue (SAR) operations.

Title: Homeowner loses RM25,000 in valuables in Bukit Antarabangsa break-in
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A homeowner lost about RM25,000 worth of valuables after a burglar broke into his house in Bukit Antarabangsa while he was at work yesterday.
Ampang Jaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid said the victim discovered the break-in after checking his home's closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage at about 4pm.
"The footage showed a Perodua Myvi stopping in front of the house in Jalan Wangsa 5, Taman Wangsa Ukay, at noon.
"A man was seen getting out of the vehicle before breaking into the house.
"The suspect fled with several watches, jewellery, a laptop and credit cards," he said in a statement today.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 457 of the Penal Code for house-breaking, which carries a maximum five-year jail term and a fine upon conviction.
The incident came to public attention after a post on Threads went viral, warning residents to be cautious and claiming that the same Myvi had been spotted in the area several weeks earlier.
The post also alleged that the vehicle had been involved in an attempted break-in at a house in Taman Melawati on Aug 4.

Title: Nearly RM1mil pumped into Gombak community, school projects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A joint programme between the Selangor government and the Higher Education Ministry has channelled nearly RM1 million in funding towards community and school development in Gombak, says Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
Amirudin, who is also Gombak MP, said the Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Madani programmes at Kampung Melayu Wira Damai and SMK Sungai Kertas respectively were implemented under the ministry's Higher Education Department, with funding from the department and private sector partners.
He said the initiatives covered infrastructure upgrades and skills development, including road works, community hall improvements, culinary and business training, as well as the setting up of a cafe.
"The programmes have brought great benefits to residents in the villages and schools, adding to their beauty, vibrancy and available infrastructure," he said after officiating the Karnival Cinta Masjid at Masjid Al-Khairiyah, Taman Seri Gombak, here.
Amirudin later said he was scheduled to visit Sekolah Agama Al-Amin, where an education carnival was being held.
"Al-Amin is a private school that has been rooted in Gombak for quite some time, producing many good and effective graduates and students for the country," he said.

Title: Haze: 10 Sarawak areas record unhealthy API readings, Serian highest at 196
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ten areas in Sarawak continued to record unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 3pm today, with Serian recording the highest reading at 196.
Based on the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, other areas recording unhealthy API readings included Kuching (188), Samarahan (178), Sri Aman (175) and Sarikei (174).
The other areas were Sibu (162), Bintulu and Mukah (157), Samalaju (155) and Miri (143).
Bukit Rambai in Melaka was the only area outside Sarawak to record an unhealthy API reading, at 152.
Yesterday,
591 schools
under 10 district education offices in Sarawak were ordered to close due to deteriorating air quality caused by transboundary haze.
The affected schools are under the Kuching, Padawan, Bau, Lundu, Samarahan, Simunjan, Serian, Sri Aman, Lubok Antu and Betong PPDs.
The Department of Environment (DOE) said the Regional Haze Map issued by the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) showed continued dry weather conditions across most of the southern Asean region, except for rainfall over northeastern Borneo and northern Sumatera.
Hotspots were detected extensively in Kalimantan, while isolated hotspots were detected in other parts of the region. Moderate to dense transboundary smoke plumes were observed in West Kalimantan and moving northwards into western Sarawak.
The DOE said it had stepped up enforcement operations and daily patrols in areas at risk of open burning while monitoring API readings.
The National Open Burning Action Plan and National Haze Action Plan have also been activated to coordinate government agencies' efforts to tackle open burning and respond to haze conditions nationwide.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are hazardous.

Title: Selangor eyes RM2.5mil upgrade for Bukit Permata Muslim cemetery
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Selangor government plans to upgrade the Bukit Permata Muslim cemetery at an estimated cost of RM2.5 million, with the project to be proposed for next year's state budget.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the upgrade was expected to take about two years to complete.
"For Bukit Permata, there is corrective work that we want to carry out.
"It will also take about two years, at a cost of around RM2.5 million. We will bring this for next year's budget, God willing," he said.
He said this after officiating the Karnival Cinta Masjid at Masjid Al-Khairiyah, Taman Seri Gombak, here.
On the ongoing development of the Sungai Kertas Muslim cemetery in Sungai Tua, Amirudin said the first phase was on track for completion in October, with subsequent phases to follow.
"We have almost completed the work in the Sungai Tua area, at Sungai Kertas.
"Phase one will be completed this October, followed by the subsequent phases," he said.

Title: Putrajaya cyclist deaths highlight need for stronger road safety measures
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The deaths of two cyclists in a late-night collision in Putrajaya on Thursday have renewed concerns over cyclist safety on public roads, with calls for stronger preventive measures involving road users, authorities and cycling groups.
Road Safety Expert Association (RSEA) founder and road safety and motorsports adviser Jamil Manan Supri said the deaths of Syazwan Zharif Abdul Karim, 30, and Mohd Hilmi Tahar, 48, should serve as a serious road safety lesson for all road users.
Jamil said preventing similar incidents required a shared effort involving cyclists, motorists, road authorities and cycling groups or event organisers.
He said cyclists faced greater risks at night as visibility and perception were significantly reduced, and called on them to use effective front and rear lights, wear high-visibility or reflective clothing, and ensure their helmets were properly fitted.
"Cyclists should ride predictably, avoid sudden changes in direction, signal before changing position and avoid unnecessarily occupying multiple lanes.
"They should also conduct basic risk assessments of their routes, while group rides should have a designated ride leader and rear sweeper to monitor the group.
"Being visible is not merely a matter of comfort; it can be the difference between being seen and being hit," he said.
Jamil also reminded motorists to anticipate vulnerable road users and not assume a road was clear simply because another vehicle or cyclist was not immediately visible.
"Before changing lanes, motorists should check their mirrors, signal, check blind spots, assess the situation and only change lanes when it is safe to do so," he said.
At night, motorists should reduce speed when visibility is limited, remain alert to cyclists and motorcyclists, avoid distractions and maintain sufficient lateral clearance from vulnerable road users.
"A driver may have the right of way in a particular situation, but the right of way does not remove the responsibility to exercise due care."
Jamil said RSEA also called for road safety and lighting audits at Km9, Jalan Persiaran Selatan, where the incident took place, as well as other routes commonly used by cyclists at night.
The audits should examine street lighting, dark spots, cyclist visibility, road markings, sight distances, road geometry, prevailing speeds and the availability of CCTV or other monitoring systems.
"Street lighting should not merely illuminate the road surface. It must enable motorists to detect road users in sufficient time to react safely," he said.
Jamil added that cycling groups and event organisers should implement minimum night-riding safety protocols, including front and rear lighting, reflective gear, pre-ride safety briefings, route risk assessments, group-size management and emergency procedures.
"Groups should also identify high-risk locations along their routes and, where possible, choose routes with adequate lighting and safer road environments."
He stressed that road safety should not become a debate over whether cyclists or motorists were to blame before investigations were completed.
"This is not a 'cyclists versus motorists' issue. Road safety is a shared responsibility.
"A cyclist cannot assume that every motorist will see them, while a motorist cannot assume that every cyclist will be highly visible.
"Both must anticipate human error and take reasonable steps to prevent a collision," he said.
Jamil said while the police investigation should determine what happened and whether any offence was committed, road safety agencies should also examine systemic factors, including road design, lighting, visibility, vehicle and cyclist behaviour, and the overall operating environment.
"We cannot bring them back to their families. But we can ensure that their deaths become a catalyst for stronger preventive measures so that the next family does not receive the same devastating news."

Title: Hiker found safe after 19 hours lost in Lambir Hills National Park
Article:
MIRI: A female hiker who spent the night lost in Lambir Hills National Park was found safe today after a 19-hour search.
Veronique Anak Joseph, 31, was found at about 11.17am after rescuers received information about her location via WhatsApp.
Rescuers said she suffered minor injuries, believed to have been caused by a fall, and was brought out of the forest before being taken to a nearby hospital for further examination.
Veronique was reported missing yesterday after becoming separated from five friends while descending from the summit.
The group began their hike at about 9am and reached the summit around noon before starting their descent at about 1pm.
At about 2pm, Veronique, who was ahead of the group, was believed to have moved faster and became separated from her friends.
Her disappearance was discovered after the other hikers reached the starting checkpoint at about 4.30pm and alerted park rangers.
Firefighters from the Miri Fire and Rescue Station, assisted by park rangers and Wildlife Guardian Rangers, were deployed for the search and rescue operation.
Search efforts were suspended last night due to darkness and uncertainty over her location, but resumed this morning and led to her discovery.
